facts: Crocs, Inc. delivered full year 2025 revenue of over $4 billion, with approximately $3.3 billion from the Crocs Brand (up 1% YoY) and $715 million from HEYDUDE (down 14% YoY).

Free cash flow generation was $659 million in 2025, enabling $128 million in debt paydown and repurchase of approximately 6.5 million shares for $577 million, representing roughly 10% of shares outstanding.
Full year 2025 adjusted diluted EPS was $12.51 (down 5% YoY), and 2026 guidance calls for adjusted diluted EPS of $12.88 to $13.35.
Crocs Brand international revenue grew 11% in 2025 on top of 19% growth the prior year, with China growing 30% and now representing approximately 8% of Crocs Brand sales.

Enterprise adjusted gross margin for full year 2025 was 58.3%, down 50 basis points YoY, driven by a 130 basis point tariff headwind, with an additional ~80 basis points of incremental tariff pressure expected in 2026.
For full year 2026, the company expects enterprise revenue growth in the range of up slightly to down 1% on a reported basis, with Crocs Brand flat to up 2% and HEYDUDE down approximately 7% to 9%.
The company identified $100 million of cost savings for 2026 (balanced between COGS and SG&A), on top of the $50 million cost savings program effectively executed in 2025.
HEYDUDE brand awareness increased 9 percentage points to 39% year-over-year, and the company expects HEYDUDE to return to revenue growth in the second half of 2026.
Adjusted operating margin was 22.3% for full year 2025 (down 330 basis points YoY), with the company expecting modest expansion from that level in 2026.
For Q1 2026, the company expects revenues down 3.5% to 5.5%, adjusted operating margin of approximately 21.5%, and adjusted diluted EPS of $2.67 to $2.77.
Q3 2025 revenue was $11.5 million, down from $11.7 million in Q2 2025.
Cash position decreased to $10.3 million from $10.5 million at the end of Q2 2025.
The company expects both revenue and adjusted EBITDA to be sequentially lower in Q4 2025 compared to Q3 2025.
Management anticipates revenue growth on a run rate basis in the 10% range from year-end levels in 2026.
The company expects adjusted EBITDA margins of 10% or more in the course of 2026.
Marchex entered an agreement in principle to acquire Archenia for a $10 million convertible promissory note plus an earn-out of up to 4 million shares over 2 years.
The combined company with Archenia would have revenue run rates of approximately $15 million quarterly or approximately $60 million annualized.
Management believes the combined company's revenue could grow in the 15% to 20% range in 2026.
The company migrated more than 1,000 customers onto its new technology platform, with completion expected by year-end 2025.
Q3 2025 sales bookings accelerated to the highest levels of the year, with management expecting this momentum to continue and compound into 2026.
Q1 2026 bottom-line results came in ahead of expectations despite softer top-line trends, with the company reaffirming its full-year 2026 guidance.

Management quantified roughly $0.02–$0.03 of EPS headwind in the back half of 2026 from oil-related cost pressures, primarily on resin/packaging and distribution, which were not anticipated when initial guidance was set.

The company is virtually fully hedged on its core program commodities for the balance of 2026, but diesel fuel is not hedged (though much of DSD fuel cost is borne by distribution partners, not on Flowers' P&L).
Management reset the dividend, freeing up approximately $100 million of cash, with deleveraging as the primary use and a target of reducing leverage below 3x by the end of fiscal 2027.

Nature's Own was relaunched nationwide with reformulation removing another one-third of ingredients, non-GMO verification, and a 360-degree marketing campaign featuring John Cena, with management cautioning a 6–12 month lag before measurable impact.

Traditional loaf, which represents roughly 38% of branded retail, remains the company's primary weak spot, and management defines success of the Nature's Own relaunch simply as stabilizing volumes in that segment.
Pricing taken late last year has left price gaps wider than desired, pressuring volume share, but where gaps have narrowed in certain channels, share trends are already improving.

Promotional and marketing spend was deliberately pulled back in Q1 to preserve dry powder for the Nature's Own relaunch, with the promotional calendar expected to normalize over the remainder of the year.
Guidance assumes no volume recovery but easier comps as the year progresses, supported by half loaf variety expansion, continued snack and Better For You growth, and SG&A cost mitigation.

FY2026 CapEx guidance of $115–$125 million breaks down to roughly $2 million per bakery for maintenance with the remainder allocated to growth initiatives including product line extensions and productivity projects.
Q3 delivered 0.5% same-store sales growth with the final 2 months averaging roughly plus 1.5% comp growth, which has accelerated into Q4.
Restaurant level operating margins reached 12.5% and EBITDA margins reached 6.4%, representing improvements of 80 and 70 basis points year-over-year respectively.
The company repurchased 996,000 common shares for $33.2 million during Q3, with a year-to-date total of 1,838,000 shares for $62.4 million.
The Board authorized an additional $75 million in share repurchases, increasing 2025 annual repurchase expectations from $45-55 million to $65-80 million.
Q3 sales reached $330 million, a 1.4% increase versus last year, with restaurant level operating profit increasing 8.8% to $41.3 million and adjusted EBITDA increasing 14.1% to $21.1 million.
Traffic in the last 6-plus weeks is tracking at roughly plus 3.5% year-on-year and close to 9% on a 2-year basis, outperforming Black Box casual dining benchmarks.
Cost of sales was 25.7% in Q3, 90 basis points favorable year-over-year, while gross margin is up 90 basis points and margin after direct labor is up 130 basis points year-over-year.
The company ended Q3 with net funded debt of $64.1 million, comprised of a debt balance of $89.5 million and cash of $25.4 million.
Management expects Q4 same-store sales growth of approximately 2% to 2.5%, which would result in full year comps of approximately 2% as guided.
The company is targeting up to 2 new restaurant openings in the second half of 2026 to pilot a refreshed prototype, having signed 2 leases with additional deals in late-stage development.

Greif lowered its fiscal 2026 low-end adjusted EBITDA guidance to $610 million (approximately $20 million reduction) to reflect direct disruption and continued volume softness from the Middle East conflict, while maintaining low-end adjusted free cash flow guidance of $315 million.
Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA improved 7.5% year-over-year with margins expanding 110 basis points YoY and 230 basis points sequentially, driving adjusted EPS growth of over 60% year-over-year.

Adjusted free cash flow improved $90 million (up 107%) versus Q2 2025, or over 200% excluding approximately $30 million of cash flow from the divested containerboard business in the prior-year period.

The Middle East conflict caused intermittent shutdowns at facilities in the region, resulting in a less-than-$5 million EBITDA hit in Q2, with steel/metal volumes most impacted and expected to remain pressured for the rest of the year.

Revised full-year volume assumptions now call for Metal, Fiber and Closures down mid-single digits and Polymers flat, versus prior guidance of metals/fiber flat to down low-singles and polymers/closures up low-singles.

Greif achieved $75 million of cost savings year-to-date and remains on track for its full-year target of $80–$90 million, within a broader $120 million commitment by fiscal year-end 2027, including a structural 12% reduction in professional workforce.

The company ended Q2 with a leverage ratio of 1.1x — described as the strongest balance sheet in its nearly 150-year history — even after completing its $150 million share repurchase program shortly after quarter-end.

An additional $300 million share repurchase authorization remains available, with management indicating intent to be regular buyers in a disciplined, value-accretive manner while maintaining leverage below 2x.
Greif refinanced its debt facilities, extending term loans to 2031 and achieving a current weighted average interest rate of 3.14%, aided by access to the Farm Credit System.

A $60/ton URB price increase was recognized by RISI in April and is expected to deliver an $11 million benefit (net $9 million after a $2 million OCC cost headwind), flowing through the P&L starting in July.

Middle East represents a mid-single-digit percentage of Coty's net revenue and was previously growing at high rates, but the late-February disruption halted sell-in in March and is expected to create a 2-to-3-point headwind in Q4.

Each $1 increase in oil prices translates to roughly a $2 million gross profit impact for Coty (before mitigation), affecting freight, glass, and plastic components, with hedging and inventory protecting the company through approximately the end of calendar year 2026.
Coty paid approximately $30 million in tariffs impacting the P&L this year, with management exploring potential refund opportunities.
The beauty market grew 5% in Q3, with both Prestige and Mass segments each growing 5%, indicating continued consumer resilience.
CoverGirl and Sally Hansen are now growing ahead of the U.S. market in unit volume and catching up in value, driven by a strategic repositioning of CoverGirl toward Gen X consumers.

European retailers overstocked for the Christmas period and worked down inventory in Q3 due to weaker-than-expected sellout, contributing to the Prestige sell-in/sellout gap along with the Middle East disruption and a highly promotional environment.

Coty is exiting the Orveda brand by the end of fiscal year 2026 (June-August), with related costs already reserved in Q2, and is also exiting smaller Consumer Beauty markets in Southeast Asia and Mexico.

Q3 A&CP spending was flat year-over-year (increasing as a percentage of revenue), with management consciously reallocating some Q3 budget toward higher-ROI Mother's Day and Father's Day Prestige campaigns.
Management categorically denied media rumors of divesting Prestige licenses such as Burberry and Hugo Boss, while remaining open to an early Gucci license exit if it creates shareholder value.
Management expects EBITDA year-over-year trend to improve over the course of fiscal 2027, though short-term benefits rolling off and potential oil-driven inflation will create headwinds.
Revenue was reported at $464.3 million, an 8.5% increase over the prior year, marking the sixth consecutive sequential revenue increase and the highest rate of growth since Q1 2018.
Q4 2025 revenue is estimated in the range of $460 million to $470 million.
Diluted earnings per share was $0.59, which includes a $0.36 per share benefit primarily related to the Employee Retention Credit (ERC), partially offset by a $0.03 Genesis charge.
Cash flow from operations was $87.1 million after adjusting for a $15.8 million decrease in payroll accrual, including a $31.8 million benefit related to ERC.
The company ended Q3 with cash and marketable securities of $207.5 million and an undrawn credit facility.
Year-to-date share repurchases totaled $42 million, with $27.3 million repurchased in Q3 under a $50 million share repurchase plan valid through June 2026.
Client retention rates are at 90% and strengthening.

Less than 15% of over 23,000 identified long-term and post-acute care facilities use a third-party for Environmental Services and less than 8% for Dining & Nutrition Services, with HCSG holding over 80% of that outsourced market.
The campus/education segment remains less than 5% of total company revenues and is the company's top M&A acquisition target.
Segment margins for Environmental and Dietary Services were reported at 10.7% and 5.1%, respectively, with each including 60 basis points of charges related to the Genesis bankruptcy.
Fiscal year 2025 revenue was $679.5 million with comparable sales declining 7.9% and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $11 million.
The company opened 35 net new restaurants in fiscal year 2025, ending the year with 281 locations, and restaurant-level margin was 15.2%.
Fourth quarter comparable sales declined 11.5%, driven by a 13.3% decrease in traffic and mix, partially offset by a 1.8% benefit from menu price increases.
January same-store sales declined 11.8% impacted by severe weather, with storms contributing approximately 320 basis points of headwind to Q1 trends through early reporting.

Fiscal year 2026 guidance calls for same-store sales decline of 2% to 4%, restaurant-level margin of 14.2% to 14.7%, adjusted EBITDA of $1 million to $6 million, and approximately 15 net new restaurant openings.

Established Infinite Kitchen locations delivered labor savings of more than 700 basis points compared to classic counterparts of similar age, with higher AUVs; the company ended the year with 30 IK locations and has since opened two more.
The company closed the sale of Spyce at the beginning of fiscal 2026, receiving $100 million in cash proceeds, supplementing the $89.2 million in cash at quarter end.

Wraps launched in a market pilot across approximately 68 restaurants in Manhattan, the Midwest, and Los Angeles, priced below $15 across all markets, with a potential mid-2026 system-wide rollout if stage-gate criteria are met.
For 2026, underlying support center (G&A) costs excluding stock-based compensation and one-time expenses are expected to be approximately 13% of revenue, down from 15.3% in 2025.

Scan-to-pay now represents approximately 20% of frontline in-store transactions, and loyalty members who transact both digitally and in-store visit nearly 2x more frequently than digital-only customers.

Halliburton delivered total company revenue of $22.2 billion for 2025 with an adjusted operating margin of 14%, generating $2.9 billion of cash flow from operations and $1.9 billion of free cash flow.
The company returned 85% of free cash flow to shareholders, including $1 billion in stock repurchases, reducing the share count to its lowest level in 10 years.
North America revenue is expected to decline high single digits in 2026, while international revenue is expected to be flat to up modestly.
Q4 2025 adjusted net income per diluted share was $0.69, with total company revenue of $5.7 billion and adjusted operating margin of 15%.
For Q1 2026, Completion and Production division revenue is expected to decrease 7% to 9% sequentially with margins declining about 300 basis points.
Customer adoption of ZEUS IQ, Sensori and auto frac technologies increased by 18% in Q4 2025.
Halliburton and VoltaGrid secured manufacturing capacity for 400 megawatts of modular power systems during the quarter.
The company expects 2026 capital expenditures of approximately $1.1 billion, excluding any capital spending for potential Venezuela reentry.
Management confirmed the Street's approximately $4 billion EBITDA estimate for 2026 is within the range of outcomes they are evaluating.
SAP migration expenses are expected to run $40-45 million per quarter through Q4 2026, with expected annual savings of approximately $100 million after project completion.
Q1 2026 revenue was $807 million, up 34% year-over-year, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of growth above 30%.
Axon raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to 30%-32% growth while maintaining the 25.5% adjusted EBITDA margin target, with Q1 adjusted EBITDA margin at 25%.

AI bookings grew 140% year-over-year and AI product revenue grew more than 700% year-over-year (off a small base), with nearly all large domestic law enforcement agencies now including AI in their purchases.
Dedrone bookings were up 500% year-over-year and total Dedrone revenue (hardware and software) grew over 300%, with management stating they are more limited by production capacity than by demand.
Software and services revenue grew 35% year-over-year to $355 million, ARR grew 35% to $1.5 billion, and net revenue retention was 125%.
Connected devices revenue grew 33% to $453 million, with Platform Solutions (including counter-drone hardware) up 95% year-over-year.
International revenue more than doubled (up over 100% year-over-year), representing 20% of total revenue, and future contracted bookings rose 44% year-over-year to $14.3 billion.
Axon closed a $40 million enterprise deal with one of the world's largest telecom providers centered on Fusus, following 50% year-over-year Q1 enterprise growth in April.

The company expects approximately $450 million of full-year 2026 free cash flow despite significant inventory investments, and projects stock-based compensation of $590M-$620M with average annual dilution kept below 2.5%.

Axon has booked over 1.5x the combined purchase price of Fusus (acquired ~2 years ago) and Dedrone (~18 months ago), and a major Mid-Atlantic city just approved a $150 million deal including the AI Era Plan.
Q3 2025 revenue was $10.1 million, representing a more than 580% increase year-over-year and nearly 60% sequential growth from Q2.
The company raised its full year 2025 revenue target to at least $36 million, implying Q4 revenue of more than $15 million.
Ondas established a 2026 revenue target of at least $110 million, which does not include any additional M&A beyond announced acquisitions.
Consolidated backlog grew to $23.3 million as of September 30, 2025, more than double from the start of the year, and exceeds $40 million when including closed or pending Q4 acquisitions.
Cash position was $433 million as of September 30, 2025, with pro forma cash of $840.4 million after the $407 million net proceeds from the October 7, 2025 equity offering.
The company raised approximately $855 million in equity during 2025 to support its growth plan.
Gross profit was $2.6 million in Q3 2025 with a 26% gross margin, compared to $0.05 million gross profit in Q3 2024.
The M&A pipeline includes over 20 companies with advanced activity on 7 potential targets, collectively representing more than $500 million in potential additional revenue.
Sentrycs has over 200 global deployments across more than 25 countries with gross margins in the upper 70% range and triple-digit compound annual growth rate in bookings.
Management expects operating businesses to reach EBITDA positive by the second half of 2026, with a target gross margin of 50%.
Net interest margin increased 8 basis points to 3.19% in Q3, with management expecting a few basis points of expansion from September's 3.16% run rate in Q4.
Net interest income was $169.3 million in Q3, up $5.7 million from the prior quarter.
Total loans declined by $223 million in Q3, driven by a $146 million decline in dealer flooring balances and approximately $130 million in C&I line paydowns.
Total deposits increased approximately $500 million in Q3, with public deposits up $406 million and commercial deposits up $135 million.
The company repurchased approximately 965,000 shares at a total cost of $24 million, with $26 million of authorization remaining under the 2025 stock repurchase plan.
Full year expenses are now expected to come in below the previous guidance of $506 million.
Net charge-offs were $4.2 million or 12 basis points of total loans in Q3, with the allowance for credit losses coverage remaining at 117 basis points.
Classified assets increased $30.1 million in Q3 due primarily to a single long-time borrower.
Management expects approximately $1 billion of fixed rate loan cash flows to reprice over the next 12 months at roughly a 125 basis point higher spread.
The rate-sensitive deposit portfolio of approximately $4.5 billion is expected to achieve around 90% beta on the next Fed rate cut, declining to approximately 85-88% on subsequent cuts.
Q3 2025 revenues were $377 million with gross profit of $66 million and net income of $22 million, representing the company's highest quarterly results since 2014.
Adjusted EBITDA was $104 million for Q3 2025, with positive operating cash flow of $24 million and positive free cash flow of $23 million.
The company had cash and cash equivalents of $338 million and total liquidity of $430 million at quarter end, with funded debt of $315 million resulting in negative net debt of $31 million.
Full-year 2025 guidance was tightened to revenues of $1.23 billion to $1.29 billion, EBITDA of $240 million to $270 million, and free cash flow of $100 million to $140 million.
Year-to-date share repurchases totaled $30 million with 4.6 million shares acquired, in line with the target of minimum 25% of expected free cash flow.
The company executed a 3-year well intervention contract with a minimum 150-day commitment for key units in the Gulf of America.
The Q7000 completed a 400-day decommissioning campaign for Shell in Brazil with 100% utilization, and continues working for Shell into Q2 2026.
Shallow water abandonment segment utilization increased to 790 days in Q3 compared to 614 days in Q2, with the Hedron heavy lift barge achieving 100% utilization.
Both Siem Helix vessels in Brazil are due for 5-year special surveys in 2026, which management stated will meaningfully impact anticipated EBITDA improvements.
The company entered a 4-year agreement with NKT for installation, operation, project engineering and maintenance of the T3600, designed to be the world's most powerful subsea trencher.
Q1 2026 total revenue grew 12% to a record $233 million, with revenue outside U.S. credit growing 20% and new initiatives generating approximately 50% of total incremental revenue.
Diluted EPS was $2.20 (or $2.25 ex-notable items, up 20%), with a $0.12 EPS benefit from a 6% share count reduction following the completed $300 million ASR.

Emerging markets total trading volumes rose 30% to record levels, generating $20 million in incremental revenue over the trailing 12 months (68% of total credit incremental variable commission revenue), though total EM fee per million declined 4% due to mix.
Total global portfolio trading ADV grew 51% to a record $1.9 billion, with U.S. credit portfolio trading market share up 100 basis points year-over-year and high-yield PT ADV up approximately 78%.
Block trading ADV grew 35% to a record $7 billion across U.S. credit, EM, and Eurobonds, with U.S. high-grade dealer algos winning 30% of block trades in March.
April U.S. high-grade market share was depressed by duplicate TRACE reports inflating volumes by up to 8%; adjusting for duplicates, estimated market share would have been ~160 basis points higher.
Operating margin expanded nearly 200 basis points to 44% on 8% non-GAAP expense growth, with headcount of 859 down 1% year-over-year.

Trailing 12-month free cash flow reached $316 million, while cash and investments fell to $537 million from $679 million at year-end 2025, and $205 million remains on the share repurchase authorization as of April 30, 2026.
Total credit fee capture declined year-over-year due to protocol and product mix shifts, partially offset by higher duration in U.S. high-grade bonds traded.

MarketAxess will pilot its new issue trading solution via a DirectBooks partnership at the end of May 2026, targeting a ~$2 trillion forecast new issue market, with click-to-trade post-break trading rolling out in the second half of 2026.
Hexcel achieved full year 2025 sales of $1.894 billion, adjusted EPS of $1.76, and free cash flow of $157 million.
For 2026, Hexcel expects sales in the range of $2.0 billion to $2.1 billion, adjusted EPS between $2.10 and $2.30, and free cash flow greater than $195 million.
The company expects to generate in excess of $1 billion in free cash flow cumulatively over the next 4 years from 2026 to 2029.
When Airbus and Boeing achieve publicly disclosed peak build rates, Hexcel expects to generate $500 million in incremental annual sales from existing sole-source contracts.
Hexcel's leverage ratio was approximately 2.7x net debt-to-EBITDA at year-end 2025 following the $350 million accelerated share repurchase program, with a target to return to 1.5-2.0x during 2026.
Fourth quarter 2025 commercial aerospace sales increased 7.6% year-over-year to $299.5 million.
The company finished 2025 with approximately 330 fewer positions compared to year-end 2024 headcount.
Since the beginning of 2024, Hexcel has returned over $800 million to stockholders through dividends and share repurchases.
The Composite Materials segment generated an adjusted operating margin of 20.5% in Q4 2025 compared to 15.3% in the prior year period.
Hexcel's underlying A350 production assumption for 2026 is approximately 80 units, up from 57 aircraft delivered by Airbus in 2025.
Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $1.16 billion, exceeding guidance, with adjusted EPS of $0.58 up 13% year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 140 bps to 17.6%.

IET delivered record bookings of $4.9 billion (third consecutive quarter above $4 billion) with a 1.5x book-to-bill, driving record RPO of $33.1 billion and IET EBITDA growth of 35% YoY to $678 million at a 20.2% margin (+310 bps).

Power Systems generated $1.4 billion in Q1 orders (~30% of total IET orders), including a 1 GW data center award, 25 BRUSH generators for Boom Supersonic (1.21 GW), and management estimates the behind-the-meter market reaching $60 billion by 2030.
LNG equipment orders totaled $1.2 billion in Q1, highlighted by a QatarEnergy award for 2 mega trains on North Field West (16 MTPA) including 6 Frame 9 turbines and 12 centrifugal compressors.
Management raised confidence that the Horizon 2 IET order target will exceed $40 billion by 2028, supported by structural energy security demand.

Baker Hughes expects approximately $3 billion in gross divestiture proceeds in 2026 from Waygate Technologies, the HMH IPO, PSI sale to Crane, and the SPC/Cactus JV, exceeding its $1 billion incremental divestment target ahead of schedule.

The Middle East conflict has taken ~10% of global oil volumes and 20% of worldwide LNG capacity offline, leading the company to revise its 2026 global upstream spending outlook to modestly below prior low-single-digit decline expectations.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for company revenue of $6.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $1.13 billion, with IET EBITDA of $670 million and OFSE EBITDA of $540 million on revenue of $3.2 billion, assuming Middle East revenue declines more than 20% sequentially.

Full-year 2026 guidance is maintained but expected to land slightly below the midpoint, with OFSE EBITDA likely at the low end of its $2.325 billion range and IET EBITDA at least the $2.7 billion midpoint.

Q1 free cash flow was $210 million, the balance sheet strengthened with net debt/EBITDA at 0.3x and a $14.8 billion cash position following a $6.5 billion U.S. bond and €3 billion inaugural European bond issuance to fund the Chart acquisition (expected to close in Q2 with $325 million targeted cost synergies).
Q1 2026 total revenue grew 23% to $93.1 million, core revenue grew 15% to $79.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA grew 57% to $24.4 million, delivering a 26% adjusted EBITDA margin.
New business commissions grew 29% in Q1, the fastest pace in nearly 5 years, while total written premiums grew 13% to $1.1 billion and policies in force grew 14% to 2 million.

Goosehead repurchased 985,000 Class A shares for $49.8 million during the quarter, funded partly by drawing $26 million on its revolver, leaving $148 million remaining on its repurchase authorization and fewer shares outstanding than at IPO.

Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance of 10%-19% organic total revenue growth and 12%-20% organic total written premium growth, and expects Q2 core revenue growth similar to Q1 after adjusting for a $4 million prior-year carrier recovery.
Client retention remained at 85% but is expected to reach 86% during 2026, with PIF growth acceleration expected to be driven more by retention improvements than new business.

Ancillary revenue (largely contingent commissions) grew 141% year-over-year to $11.9 million in Q1, with full-year contingent commission guidance unchanged at 60-85 basis points of total written premiums.

The digital agent platform now offers digital home insurance in Texas via SageSure and Mercury, in addition to 4 auto carriers (Progressive, Liberty Mutual, Mercury, Root), with carriers indicating willingness to pay outsized compensation for policies distributed via the partner/digital agent channel.

AI assistant Lily fully resolves ~19% of inbound calls without live-agent transfer, and intelligent case routing has allowed ~40 full-time service team members to be reinvested into more complex interactions.

Enterprise sales team generated new business growth of over 70% and contributed approximately 20% of new business commissions/agency fees, with partnerships covering 2.3 million mortgage origination/servicing clients and 4 million other home and financial services clients.

Texas concentration declined to 37% of premium from 39% at year-end 2025, supported by 3 new corporate offices opened in Q1 (Seattle, D.C., Minneapolis) plus Indianapolis in April, and more than half of corporate agents are now outside Texas.
Q3 subscription revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $286.3 million, exceeding the high end of guidance.
Confluent Cloud revenue grew 24% year-over-year to $161 million, representing 56% of subscription revenue.
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 340 basis points to a record 9.7%, exceeding guidance by 270 basis points.
Late-stage pipeline (dollar value of new use cases moving into production) grew more than 40% sequentially for the second consecutive quarter.
Q3 Flink ARR for Confluent Cloud grew more than 70% sequentially, with over 1,000 customers now using Flink.
$100,000+ ARR customer count increased by 48 customers quarter-over-quarter to 1,487, the largest sequential increase in 2 years.
RPO grew 43% year-over-year, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of RPO growth acceleration.
Net retention rate stabilized at 114%, while gross retention rate remained close to 90%.
A large AI native customer is moving from Confluent Cloud to self-hosted, creating a low single-digit impact to Q4 cloud revenue.
Q4 subscription revenue guidance of $295.5-296.5 million represents approximately 18% growth, with cloud revenue expected to be approximately $165 million (20% growth).

Q1 2026 total revenue grew 26% year-over-year to $60.1 million, with platform revenue up 36% to $50.9 million while volume-based revenue declined 12% to $9.2 million primarily due to lower gain share.

Net income reached $12.6 million ($0.31 EPS), up 56% year-over-year from $8.1 million ($0.21 EPS), with operating profit of approximately $15 million up 75% from $8.6 million in the prior-year quarter.

Backlog ended the quarter at $246 million, up 9% versus the same quarter last year, supported by multiple large bookings including a double-digit million-dollar Exensio Test Operations deal and an enterprise-wide Exensio Test deployment at a large IDM.

Gross margin was 76% (vs. 77% prior quarter) and operating margin was 25% (vs. 24% prior quarter and 18% year-ago), with management indicating faster-than-expected progress toward long-term targets of 77% gross margin and 27% operating margin.
Management reconfirmed full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance consistent with its 20% long-term target.

PDF shipped 1 eProbe in Q1 (contributing to revenue starting in Q2) and remains on track to ship 6 eProbe machines in 2026, with about 2 going to net new customers, 4 to existing customers, and 1 used as a demo machine.
The company expects to roughly double its eProbe subscription installed base by year-end 2026 to approximately 10 subscription machines (out of 12 total installed), versus 6 machines exiting 2025.

Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments declined to $31 million from $42 million, with roughly $10 million used for CapEx primarily on eProbe builds; the company expanded its revolver with $30 million now available and expects cash to grow in H2 2026.

CEO highlighted this as the most interesting business environment in his 100 quarters at PDF, citing CEO-level customer engagement on AI in manufacturing and an AI-enabled Exensio analytics system on track for beta release in Q3 2026.

SecureWISE is expanding beyond equipment vendors into fabs (including Intel standardizing on it), with pilots underway at OSATs and fabless customers, and equipment companies now represented in PDF's top 5 customers by bookings.
Markel Group's adjusted operating income was $2.3 billion in 2025, up 10% from $2.1 billion in 2024.
Markel Insurance delivered a combined ratio of 92.9% in Q4 2025, a 3-point improvement from 95.9% in Q4 2024, and a full-year combined ratio of 94.6%, improving 1 point from the prior year.
The exit of Global Reinsurance and the Hagerty fronting transition will decrease underwriting gross written premiums by approximately $2 billion in 2026.
The Financial segment generated $327 million in adjusted operating income, up 25% from 2024, driven by increased ILS performance fees and higher program services premium volumes.

Operating cash flow grew to $2.8 billion in 2025 from $2.6 billion in 2024, and the company returned over $1 billion to shareholders through $430 million in share repurchases and $600 million in preferred stock redemptions.

The public equity portfolio returned 10.5% for 2025 with a year-end market value of $13 billion and an unrealized gain of $8.9 billion, underperforming the S&P 500's 15% annualized return over the trailing 5-year period (12% vs 15%).
Markel Insurance's International division grew gross written premium by 14% for the year and posted an 83% combined ratio, with Asia Pacific up over 30% and European Union up 20%.
